qualification: Intel guest write, fsync and verification across full platform cold boots

intel_receipt.scope: Single guest, two complete platform cold boots; no concurrent isolation or guest lifecycle reset claim

observations: The first Linux guest verified a zero-filled block at offset 8192, wrote 4096 bytes of 0x5a and required fsync success.
After each QEMU instance exited, the host compared all 32 MiB against the expected image, including both initial qualification markers and all untouched zero padding.
The second instance opened the same medium read-only, verified the persisted block and completed the userspace syscall and bidirectional console proof.
Writer and verifier initramfs hashes matched independent Spark builds. No Intel qualification QEMU remained after completion.
limitations: One guest across full platform cold boots; guest lifecycle reset and concurrent-client isolation remain unqualified.
Successful Linux fsync and cold-boot persistence are observed; physical power-loss durability was not exercised.
Pinned Debian acceptance, canonical integration, GUI qualification and the v0.4 release remain incomplete.
